paragraphs: Avimi studied Menachot at Rav Chisda’s academy. He had not learned it from him, but recited it before him to recall it well; Rav Chisda learned from Avimi. If Rav Chisda was his student, why did he not send for him? He thought this would help more. In She'iltot: Avimi, Rav Chisda’s son, as in Arakhin, chapter Shum Hayetomim, and first chapter of Menachot, where Rav Chisda said, “I received good blows from Avimi over this teaching.” End of Yuchasin. I will copy the Gemara’s wording before you and you will see his error; I do not know what spirit passed over him. Arakhin 22a: Rav Chisda said in Avimi’s name that the law is a sixty-day appraisal. Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin sat reporting this teaching. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak asked, “But Rabbi Meir said thirty days!” He answered, “Thus Rav Chisda said: I received good blows from Avimi over this teaching.” (Rashi explains: great blows, for he taught me that the orphans’ appraisal is sixty days according to Rabbi Meir, and I objected that Rabbi Meir said thirty. He told me: continuous announcement, thirty days; on Mondays and Thursdays, sixty. End quotation.) Menachot 7a: Rabbi Avimi studied Menachot at Rav Chisda’s academy. The Gemara asks: did Avimi study there? Rav Chisda said he received good blows from Avimi, etc. (Thus Rav Chisda was Avimi’s student—Rashi.) It answers: Avimi had lost the tractate of Menachot from memory and came before Rav Chisda to recall the teaching. Why not send Rav Chisda to come to him? He thought this would help more (Rashi: because ‘you have labored and found’). Your eyes see Rav Chisda was Avimi’s student; how could he write that Avimi was Rav Chisda’s son? If he meant he saw in She'iltot that Avimi was Rav Chisda’s son—even though we have not found Rav Chisda had a son Avimi (see the entry Rav Chisda for his sons’ names)—perhaps another Rav Chisda had a son named Avimi. In citing the passages of Shum Hayetomim and Menachot, “Rav Chisda said: good blows,” he understood Rav Chisda as saying Avimi received the blows, Avimi being his son and Rav Chisda striking him. Far be such an interpretation; this is clear. He met Rav Nachman (Menachot there). Rav Chisda said in Avimi’s name: Sukkah 16b; Sotah 9a; Zevachim 26a; Menachot 77b; Arakhin 5b; Bava Kamma 13b; Sanhedrin 15a, 81b. Rav Yehudah said in Avimi’s name, Eruvin 24a. In chapter 4 of Shabbat “Abaye said” is an error for Avimi. Mar Yehudah in Avimi’s name, Chullin 48a; Ulla bar Menashya in Avimi’s name.
